title: Quant+Batched Fleet Stress Matrix (Hybrid policies)
summary: Working simulation sheet: maps regional GPU pools to quantization and batching knobs, gives stress estimates (utilization, tokens/sec) and expected model quality impact for hybrid routing policies. Use for sensitivity planning and reserve sizing ahead of Q2 promotions.
content:
Purpose:
- Quick experimentation surface to compare how mixed quantization (4-bit/8-bit/FP16) + multi-size batching affects throughput and perceived quality across regions and GPU types.
- Designed for ops/infra + solutions-eng to size reserved capacity with fallbacks and pre-warm strategies.

Assumptions and model: (short)
- Baseline model (v1.3) reference in FP16 on A100: median p95 token-latency for 512 contexts = 90ms
- Quantized variants: 8-bit (q8) latency ~1.15x FP16; 4-bit (q4) latency ~0.85x FP16 for short sequences but degrades quality by measured eval delta.
- Batching behavior: small batches (b<=8) prioritize latency, large batches (b>=32) prioritize throughput; continuous batching gives better utilization for steady traffic.
- Prefix/KV cache hit reduces effective latency by 20–45% depending on sequence reuse.

How to use this sheet:
- Rows are scenarios per region/GPU/model variant. Toggle 'batch_policy' and 'prefill_cache_rate' to see utilization impact.
- Reference the scenario notes (bottom) for quick mitigations and fallback sequences.

Key findings (summary bullets):
- Mixed pools (poolA: 60% A100-FP16, poolB: 40% A100-q4) reduce cost per token by ~30% at 70% utilization but increase regression risk on long-form prompts (>2% quality drop for abstractive summarization tests).
- Latency-sensitive routes should keep a small hot FP16 corridor (<=10% capacity) to meet p95 SLOs under burst.
- Regional pre-warm (30s) reduces cold-start tail latency and allows aggressive quantization to be used more often without SLO violations.
- Batch size tuning per route (auto-tune window 2m) recovered ~12% tokens/sec vs static config in mixed-traffic traces.

Immediate recommendations:
- Reserve an extra 12% headroom in EU-West to support Q2 campaign (conservative estimate from scenario #3).
- Add an automated canary that routes new quant profiles to 5% of traffic with replayed prompts and quality hooks.
- Add metric: quant_profile_quality_delta(percent) per model+dataset to drive rollout decisions.

Notes on quality measurement:
- We use rouge/bertscore + a human-sampled binary accept/reject on 1k prompts per week.
- Flagging threshold currently set at 1.5% average quality delta over baseline for rollback.

Limitations:
- This simulation uses synthetic arrival patterns derived from April 2025 traces; may underrepresent marketing-driven bursts.
- Some model-architecture-specific quant effects not captured (e.g., rotary embedding edge cases).

Contact: Priya for infra knobs, Zoe for eval harness, Liam for regional capacity inputs.

scenario_notes: S1: Baseline latency corridor keeps interactive apps within p95 100ms when cache hits >=35%.
S2: q8 shows modest latency increase but much better numeric stability vs q4 — use for general background workloads.
S3: q4 at scale yields highest tokens/sec but measurable ROUGE drop for long-form summarization; pair with human-in-the-loop checks.
S4: APAC H100 pool needs aggressive pre-warm and smaller batch targets to control tail latency during business hours.
S7: Global burst scenario models traffic spikes and fallback to lower-quality variants when primary pools saturate.
footnotes: This sheet is exploratory. Final reserve commitments should be validated with 48h live canary and replayed historical peaks. For legal/regional compliance, coordinate with privacy team before moving production traffic to dedicated private pools.
